prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a tiered indoor scene where the camera wearer's own hands, legs, and foreground items on a checkered mat (two white electrical switchboards, red-handled pliers, a yellow screwdriver, a smartphone, and a red Finolex wire box at the bottom right) are brightest and closest at about 0.3–0.8 m, within the wearer's immediate arm's reach. Slightly farther in front (roughly 0.9–1.5 m) and about 0.5 m beyond the foreground tools, one person lies horizontally across the left-center floor in white trousers with bare feet pointing right, while a second standing person in grey trousers and a dark shirt bends over from the upper right (around 0.8–1.6 m away) with their torso facing toward the camera wearer and their head cropped out above the frame. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera tilts up and then down while the standing person reaches forward and downward in frames 1–4—bringing their bright right arm and hand holding yellow screwdrivers to within 0.6–0.9 m of the camera and within arm's reach of the lying person's ankles—before straightening and stepping slightly back and right in frame 5 alongside a third person's lower legs on the far right (~1.5–1.8 m). Behind them at roughly 1.8–2.5 m, plastic bags (white, red, blue) on the floor, a clear water bottle behind the standing person's legs, and a red suitcase with backpacks on a recessed left shelf appear as darker grey regions partially occluded by the standing person's limbs. The depth map clarifies the 3D separation between the standing person's overarching arm and the lying person's legs underneath—which overlap visually in the 2D RGB view—Confirming the arm is tens of centimetres closer to the camera, though it is unreliable on flat foreground items like the switchboards and pliers that blend into the mat's depth plane and in the upper-left background of frames 1–2 where depth saturates to black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map partitions the scene into coarse regions, grouping the foreground checkered mat and floor (~0.4–1.5 m from the camera wearer) along with the lying person's white-trousered legs (~1.0–1.5 m) into large 'bed' masks in frames 1, 2, and 5, while isolating the camera wearer's own hands/legs and smartphone (~0.3–0.6 m, within the wearer's reach) at the bottom edge and the standing person on the right (~0.8–1.6 m, within reach of the floor items and the lying person's feet) as 'person'. In frames 2–4, the standing person's pink 'person' mask captures their bent torso, legs, and extended arms facing toward the camera wearer and reaching down in front of the lying person's feet, while frame 3 also segments the red bag on the left background shelf (~2.0 m away, ~0.8 m left of the standing person) as 'suitcase'. By frame 5, as the standing person straightens up, the map separates two sets of standing legs at the top right (~1.4–1.8 m away and ~0.3 m apart, facing left/front with upper bodies out of view) as distinct 'person' instances with a 'bottle' (~1.7 m) between them, while the foreground electrical switchboard and smartphone (~0.4–0.6 m) are labeled as 'remote' (frame 2) and 'book' (frame 5). Compared to RGB alone, the instance masks sharply delineate the occluding silhouette of the standing person's limbs against the cluttered background bags and floor, especially during the low-angle views of frames 3 and 4. However, the map is highly unreliable across frames: it completely misses the background and lying person in frames 3–4 (leaving them black), merges the lying person into the 'bed' mask, and misclassifies the lying person's bare feet as a 'cat' and the wearer's smartphone as a 'book' in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the strip, detecting only sparse 2D keypoints for the standing person in the middle frames while failing to register the camera wearer in the immediate foreground (~0.3–0.6 m), the person lying horizontally on the floor (~1.0–1.5 m), or the additional standing person on the far right in frame 5 (~1.5–1.8 m). In frame 2, a yellow torso-and-arm skeleton appears in the upper-right quadrant alongside a magenta hand skeleton (~0.8–1.0 m from the camera wearer), and in frames 3 and 4, two magenta hand skeletons are tracked in the upper-center/right area (~0.8–1.3 m away and ~0.2–0.4 m apart) as the standing person faces the camera wearer with their head occluded by the top frame boundary. Across frames 2 to 4, these magenta hand skeletons shift downward toward the floor, capturing the spatial trajectory of the standing person's left and right hands reaching down to the lying person's ankles before disappearing in frame 5 when the person steps back. While the magenta hand skeletons in frames 3 and 4 help isolate the exact positions and finger orientations of both hands holding small yellow screwdrivers against the similarly toned floor and legs in RGB, the pose map is largely unreliable here because heavy cropping of upper bodies and self-occlusion cause complete misses in frames 1 and 5 and an anatomically distorted yellow body wireframe in frame 2.
